title: Tendrilio Command Envelope v1
description: Signed, short-TTL, idempotent Command Request envelope. Actuating commands are CLIENT-signed: the cloud verifies and relays them and holds no key that can originate one. Write-back commands (v1.2.0, additive) may instead be CLOUD-signed with the platform 'cloud' variant — schema-restricted to class 'write-back', so a compromised cloud still cannot mint an actuating command (FR18: write-backs are session-gated, and silent web signing is impossible since WebAuthn requires a user gesture). Cloud signing: ECDSA P-256, DER signature (base64) over the SHA-256 envelope-hash digest (compact sorted-key JSON of the signed fields; KMS DIGEST mode); 'challenge' is a fresh nonce with no server-side consumption semantics for platform 'cloud'. The hub independently re-verifies signature (enrolled instance / command-passkey public key, or the provisioned cloud write-back public key), TTL, idempotency, and its Remote-Command Guards before acting. Reads have no envelope. See SPEC.md for semantics.

v.description: Envelope schema version. Always 1 for this document.

command_id.description: UUIDv7 idempotency key, generated by the client. A hub that has already seen this command_id must not act twice; user-initiated retry reuses it.

hub_id.description: Target Hub's cloud identifier (UUIDv7). Equals the Hub's IoT Thing name, so cert policy scoping (tendrilio/*/{hub_id}/#) and topic grammar agree.

class.description: Command class. 'actuating' moves hardware: attestation (mobile) or command-passkey Step-Up (web) required. 'write-back' is non-actuating state sync (e.g. alert acknowledge/dismiss): session-gated, no Step-Up, still enveloped, audited, and subject to the Kill Switch.

target.description: What the action applies to, using hub vocabulary verbatim: a device_id for actuator commands, a rule identifier for rule.test, an alert identifier for write-backs.

action.description: Dot-namespaced verb, lowercase snake_case (e.g. actuator.start, rule.test, alert.acknowledge). The envelope carries the verb; REST paths never do.

params.description: Action-specific parameters (snake_case keys). May be empty. Hub-side Guards validate semantics; this schema only fixes the shape.

issued_at.description: Client clock at signing: ISO 8601 UTC, millisecond precision, Z suffix. TTL is evaluated against the verifier's clock with this as the start point.

ttl_s.description: Envelope time-to-live in seconds (~30s nominal). Expired envelopes are rejected by cloud and hub alike. Named ttl_s per the contract's _s duration-suffix convention.

challenge.description: Opaque server-issued challenge bound into the signed payload. Single-use; the cloud rejects envelopes whose challenge it did not issue or has already consumed.

signature.description: Proof that an authorized credential signed THIS envelope: the owner's enrolled device credential (ios/android/web), or — for class 'write-back' only — the cloud's write-back signing key ('cloud', v1.2.0). Exactly one platform variant; variants are closed (no field mixing).

uuidv7.description: RFC 9562 UUIDv7, lowercase only (generators must emit lowercase).

base64url.description: base64url without padding (RFC 4648 §5), as used by WebAuthn JSON.

instance_id.description: The enrolled Attested App Instance whose App Attest key produced the assertion.

assertion.description: App Attest assertion (CBOR, base64-encoded) over the envelope hash — a per-request hardware signature.

instance_id.description: The enrolled Attested App Instance whose hardware-backed Keystore key (Key Attestation chain verified at enrollment) produced the signature.

signature.description: Keystore signature (base64) over the envelope hash.

play_integrity_token.description: Fresh Play Integrity verdict token whose nonce derives from the same envelope hash — binding the verdict to this command.

cloud_signature.description: v1.2.0 (additive; CONTRACT_VERSION stays 1): the cloud's own write-back signing proof. Valid ONLY when class is 'write-back' (enforced by the schema's if/then). The hub verifies against the cloud write-back public key provisioned to it (22.11).

key_id.description: Identifier of the cloud signing key (e.g. the KMS alias), so the hub can select the right provisioned public key and rotation is expressible.

signature.description: ECDSA P-256 DER signature (base64) over the SHA-256 envelope-hash digest.

credential_id.description: WebAuthn credential ID of the command passkey, registered with the API's own registry (never Cognito).

client_data_json.description: WebAuthn clientDataJSON (base64url); its challenge field carries this envelope's challenge.
